1 هَدَجَ , aor.
هَدِجَ , inf. n. هَدَجَانٌ (S, K) and هُدَاجٌ (K) and هَدْجٌ, (TA,) (tropical:) He walked gently, in a weak manner: (TA:) or he walked in the manner of an old man; (S, K;) and the like: (TA:) or he (an old man) walked with short steps: or walked hastily, without desiring to do so: (TA:) or he walked with unintermitting steps: (As:) or he walked in a shaking manner, by reason of old age. (IAar.) ―
-b2- هَدَجَ, (S,) aor.
هَدِجَ , inf. n. هَدَجَانٌ; and ↓ استهدج ; (TA;) He (an ostrich) walked, or went, (or ran, TA,) in a tremulous manner. (S, TA.) ―
-b3- هَدَجَتِ القِدْرُ (tropical:) The cooking-pot boiled vehemently. (TA.) ―
-b4- هَدَجَتْ, (S,) inf. n. هَدَجٌ, (L,) She (a camel) yearned towards her young one; حَنَّتْ عَلَى وَلَدِهَا; (S, L;) as also ↓ تهدّجت ; (L;) [and, app., uttered the cry produced by yearning towards her young one: see below:] or the latter signifies she was affectionate to her young one. (S, K.) ―
-b5- Also, inf. n. as above, (assumed tropical:) It (the wind) made a sound; syn. حَنَّتْ and صَوَّتَتْ; from هدجت النّاقة. (L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
